issues.status: Explicit principal strip-maximum conclusion disproved for a fully admissible ensemble.

source_location.claim: Theorem2.3(2.7) with En(2.5); Psi(2.20)–(2.21); real lower-bound proof chain.

issues.hypotheses: Independent real N(0,1/n) entries; all Definition2.1 moment conditions. Choose alpha=1/4,r=1/2,epsilon=1/sqrt2−3/5>0. The strip is nonempty for all sufficiently large n.
issues.suspect_step: En=n phi−(1/4)logq, q=4(Imz)^2+n^-1, is combined with a strip-maximum leading coefficient1/sqrt2 independently of alpha.
issues.decisive_evidence: Principal-minor orthogonality gives E|det(X−zI)|²=n!n^-n sum_{j=0}^n(n|z|²)^j/j!<=C sqrt(n)exp[n(|z|²−1)]. For F=e^-n(|z|²−1)|p|², the holomorphic gauge p(w)exp[-n conjugate(z)(w−z)] and disk submean give sup_strip F<=en/pi int_enlarged_strip F. Its area is O(n^-alpha), so E supF<=C n^(3/2−alpha). Since exp[2(P−En)]=F sqrt(q) and q<=17n^-2alpha, P(max(P−En)>=a logn)<=C n^(3/2−2alpha−2a). With a=3/5 the exponent is−1/5. The theorem's two-sided event is a subset, so its probability tends to0, not1.
counterevidence_and_alternatives: This proof controls the continuum maximum and does not rely on a fixed-point mean heuristic or a grid regularity assumption.
Source(2.8), mean(4.3), AppendixE and conversion(10.27)–(10.28) support the intended opposite centering sign; their internal consistency does not rescue the printed theorem.
No conflicting alternative definition of phi, variance scale or allowed real ensemble occurs on the actually viewed main-result pages.
The same printed formulas remain on retained later-v3 p12; no journal-final equivalence asserted.

repair.verified_scope: Centering algebra and compatibility with selected internal formulas. A corrected maximum law and all proof dependencies are not independently proved. A coefficient1/sqrt2−alpha with old centering follows only conditionally if the corrected theorem is established.
